verdict.rationale: The first-party evidence shows only developer building blocks for an assistant: an SDK tool-calling loop and a `RunAnywhere.voice` session that developers wire into their own apps. Nothing documents a built-in assistant inside RunAnywhere that users can hand tasks to. The only sign of an assistant that takes actions is community hands-on reports about rcli, and those describe it claiming success on actions that never ran, so they cannot stand in for a documented capability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
